page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance utilizing a constrained-core architecture designed for workloads requiring substantial RAM relative to processor count. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, the system assigns 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 256 GB of RAM, offering a high allocation of 32 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources also include 1288 GB of local SSD storage managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, while omitting discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reflects mid-tier performance across general compute and memory tasks. The instance records a Geekbench single-core score of 1272.0, a multi-core score of 4842.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 8664.65. Memory bandwidth reaches 44.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 31.87 GB/sec for writes, supporting 7.09 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Due to the limited physical core count of four cores, throughput-intensive parallel tasks exhibit bottlenecks, evidenced by weaker results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 28.53 GB/sec and lower performance in CPU-based machine learning inference.

The constrained-core layout provides qualitative cost efficiency for software applications governed by per-core licensing structures, such as commercial relational database management systems. Coupling 256 GB of memory with 1288 GB of fast local SSD storage enables extensive in-memory state retention alongside fast local scratch space. As a result, the instance is well suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, enterprise database servers, and memory-heavy ETL processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 256 GB of system memory and 1288 GB of local SSD storage, without discrete graphics processing hardware. Designed with a substantial 32 GB RAM per vCPU allocation, it addresses memory-intensive enterprise tasks while constraining processor core count for per-core software licensing efficiency. Benchmark performance shows solid mid-tier execution across single-core and multi-core evaluations, achieving 7.09 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 44.52 GB/sec large-block read memory bandwidth. Conversely, compute-heavy parallel workloads like multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and CPU-based machine learning inference show weaker results due to restricted core counts. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, large cache layers, enterprise relational databases, and data transformation pipelines.
